title: Provenance & Playback Audit — Constraint Scoring Design Notes
content:
Purpose

Short: capture a pragmatic plan for provenance-tagged scoring, deterministic playback for audits, and compact explainability logs that support cross-region arbitration without exploding storage costs. This doc is intentionally implementation-sketchy and focused on operational tradeoffs — not the full formal spec.

Background / motivation

We need:
- deterministic, replayable scoring for policy decisions so SRE/GTM/customer-support can reproduce a decision made weeks ago;
- compact explain logs that contain enough context for debugging and quality analysis but small enough to retain across regions for 90 days;
- cross-region conflict resolution for constraints and scoring heuristics when control plane updates are eventual;
- a playback harness that can run decisions against (a) exact historical request, (b) request with canonicalized external signals (rate limits, quotas), and (c) synthetic perturbations to evaluate sensitivity.

Principles / constraints

1) Determinism over micro-optimizations — scoring must be determinable from recorded inputs + minimal runtime context. Avoid coupling to ephemeral runtime state when possible.
2) Keep provenance explicit — every score delta includes a provenance tag (source, actor, version, timestamp).
3) Explainability logs are first-class, but store a summarized index for long-term storage and a full extended blob for the audit window.
4) Multi-region correctness: control-plane rollouts may be asynchronous; we must be able to calculate "decision lineage" and run deterministic arbitration during playback.

Key concepts and fields

- request_snapshot (string id) — reference to the canonical request payload and headers used for decisioning.
- scoring_vector (array of floats) — the raw contributions (we store an indexed stringified array in short-term logs; index -> name mapping is in metadata).
- score_provenance (list of strings) — ordered list of provenance tags e.g. "policy:constraint:v2.3:user-overrides:2026-02-10T12:02:03Z". Each tag is stable and maps to a control-plane artifact id.
- decision_trace_id (string) — pseudo-UUID linking to traces across services (APIGW -> router -> evaluator -> serving).
- compact_explain (string) — 1–2 line human-friendly summary (used in UIs / incident emails).
- explain_blob_uri (string) — pointer to full JSON blob stored in cold storage for audit window.

Logging schemas (examples)

Short-line log (emitted inline, high-cardinality):
TIMESTAMP | TRACE_ID | REQ_SNAP_ID | DECISION:ALLOW|DENY|FALLBACK | TOP_CONTRIBS:idx1=+0.12,idx7=-0.34 | PROV=policy:v2.3;rb:canary;region:us-east1

Extended explain blob (persisted to explain_blob_uri) contains: request_snapshot, full scoring_vector, feature_hashes (redacted as necessary), rule-eval-timings, provenance_tags expanded to artifact metadata, fallback history.

Provenance model and control-plane mapping

- Control plane artifacts (constraint definitions, score weights, fallbacks, aggregation rules) are assigned immutable artifact IDs (AID) on write. A single human-change generates a new AID.
- Each runtime decision references the set of AIDs that were read during evaluation in a stable, ordered way. This list is the minimal provenance.
- During playback, we fetch the AIDs referenced by the recorded decision and either:
  a) replay with the same artifact definitions (fast path), or
  b) if the artifact was deleted/rotated, use the archived artifact snapshot from control-plane history to reconstruct semantics.

Cross-region arbitration model

Problem: a policy change (e.g., tightening a constraint) may be written in region A and applied earlier there than in region B. Live requests can see different behavior depending on which control-plane replica they hit. We must be able to:
- tag decisions with region-scoped control-plane frontier;
- let playback emulate both the local-region state and a global-serial view for incident analysis.

Design: each decision record has control_plane_frontier: {region_ts_map} where region_ts_map is a small map of region->AID-ingest-ts (we store as string list like "us-east1:2026-02-10T12:02:03Z" to avoid nested objects). Playback options: local, global-serial, or tolerant (apply later-writes as fallbacks).

Scoring delta approach (how to store cheaply)

Instead of storing full float vectors long-term, we:
- store dense vectors for the audit window (30 days) in S3 with fast lookup by req_snap_id;
- for longer retention, compress to top-k contributions + checksum of the full vector (enables verifying a reconstructed vector matches the archived checksum).
- keep index->feature mapping versioned in control-plane so that the indices remain stable across time.

Playback harness: modes and expected outputs

Modes:
- deterministic-replay: use recorded AIDs + archived artifacts -> must reproduce identical decision and score.
- comparative-replay: run the same request against current control-plane artifacts and surface diffs in score_provenance and final outcome.
- sensitivity-sweep: perturb a small set of features/weights to measure decision boundary (used for regression alerts).

Output: pass/fail (match), diff report (delta per contribution), provenance delta (which AIDs differ). Store playback-run metadata as a new small record that references original decision_trace_id.

Operational considerations

Retention and cost:
- default: 90d full explain_blob, 365d compact index, checksum stored for 5y. This balances customer audit needs and cloud cost.
- cold archive of old artifacts (AIDs) in bucket lifecycle for 7 years for enterprise compliance requests.

Backfills and schema migrations:
- record schema version on every decision (explain_schema_v1, v2, ...). Playback harness supports migrating v1->v2 in memory using transformation functions.
- when modifying scoring index mapping, create a compatibility layer that can remap old indices to new feature names via control-plane index-mapping artifacts.

Rollout & testing plan (short)

1) Implement artifact AID history store + read API (immutable snapshots). Unit tests for snapshot retrieval.
2) Emit compact_explain + provenance tags inline for 10% traffic. Validate sizes and retention metrics.
3) Build playback harness (deterministic mode) against archived AIDs. Run on sampled 1% of traffic to validate reproducibility.
4) Expand to 100% traffic after 90d of validated parity.

Open questions / TODOs

- How to redact PII from explain_blob while keeping deterministic replay? Need policy for canonicalized redaction + canonicalization logs.
- Storage budget: what is the S3 spend cap for long-tail customers? Do we tier retention by customer SLA?
- Tighten region frontier representation: can we compress region_ts_map further while keeping enough fidelity for arbitration?
- Define exact API contract for archived artifact retrieval (latency SLOs).

Appendix: quick-play examples

1) Example short-line log:
2026-02-12T14:03:01Z | TRACE=3b2a... | REQ=rsnap:84af | DECISION=DENY | TOP=3:+0.76,7:-0.44 | PROV=aid:policy-constraints:v3.1;aid:weight-set:v5

2) Minimal playback pseudocode:
function playback(decision_record, mode):
  aids = parse(decision_record.provenance_tags)
  artifacts = controlplane.fetch(aids, mode) // mode chooses archived vs live resolution
  result = evaluator.evaluate(decision_record.request_snapshot, artifacts)
  return {match: result.outcome == decision_record.outcome, diff: result.score - decision_record.score}

End of doc.
